answer_1.quote: We experiment with pre-trained sequence-to-sequence models , generating either a sequence of questions or a single question using nucleus sampling over multiple rounds.

answer_2.quote: We also explored an automated method for assessing whether generated questions match ground truth ones. ... we rely on existing scoring functions that can compare single strings, like ROUGE and BERTScore.

answer_4.quote: We conduct a user study in which we ask an annotator to rate how useful a set of questions (without answers) are to determine the veracity of a claim.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators score sets of subquestions on a Likert scale from 1 to 5, where 1 denotes that knowing the answers to the questions does not help at all and 5 denotes that they can accurately judge the claim once they know the answer.
